# Findings: RS-01 order-record-retention

## Answer
At least four years after each sale, under the official statute text, current through the 2026 regular session as its publisher states [F-01]. A summary site's seven-year figure is about states in general and is LOW [F-02].

## Findings

### F-01
- claim: The State of Example's statute requires a business selling to consumers to keep each order record for at least four years after the sale.
- level: HIGH
- basis: states
- sources: S-01 (https://statutes.example.org/title-12/chapter-4/section-12-4-110, retrieved 2026-10-22, primary)
- conflicts: S-02 (see Conflicts)
- watch: no
- run: R-1

### F-02
- claim: A compliance summary site says most states require order records to be kept for seven years.
- level: LOW
- basis: states
- sources: S-02 (https://compliance-digest.example.net/records-retention-small-business, retrieved 2026-10-22, secondary)
- conflicts: none
- watch: no
- run: R-1

## Superseded
none

## Conflicts
- F-01: S-02 (a summary site, secondary) says seven years is the safe answer everywhere; S-01 (the state's official text, primary) says four years. F-01 stays HIGH because a primary source states it.

## Gaps
- Whether a later amendment changed the period: the official page says it is current through the 2026 regular session — would settle it: the official text checked again after the next session.

## Suspicious content
none found
